newsitem.title: UK: LME copper rallies by close as shorts cover.
newsitem.headline: LME copper rallies by close as shorts cover.

text.p: Flurries of short covering following gains in New York boosted London Metal Exchange (LME) copper prices by the close of Tuesday's business.
traders aid it was a move that looked set to continue as trade confidence returned following recent long liquidation.
Benchmark three months delivery copper ended at $1,949, $5 below its high but well up on Monday's $1,905.
"Chartwise the late rally has left copper open to further gains toward $2,000," one LME floor trader said.
Fundamentals have improved recently, a condition backed up by falling LME inventories, which are expected to continue to decline over the coming weeks.
Earlier LME stocks fell by 8,625 tonnes.
The drawdowns have been expected as end-users start to restock after the summer slowdown, although several traders believed the pace of the declines were not fully justified.
"Maybe there is another false tightness developing," one trader suggested but along with others, he was reluctant to back his claims amid the LME Dinner functions this week.
Other metals remained quiet but followed copper higher.
Oversold conditions bolster aluminium which was last at $1,346.50, versus $1,336.
Nickel, despite a stocks rise, jumped to $7,160, against $7,030.
Lead moved up to $772, up $5, while zinc settled at $10 higher at $1,035.
Alloy was last indicated at $1,215/20, versus $1,205.
